content.subject: Move misleading "Saving nickname changes" log into closure body
content.description:
`nickname_field.rs:60` has `info!("Saving nickname changes");` inside the closure-creation block (around `let save_changes = { info!(...); ... move |new_value| { ... } }`), so it fires on every component re-render — i.e. every keystroke in the nickname input — not on actual saves. The 30+ log entries we saw in the verification logcat were all spurious re-renders, not actual save attempts.

Fix: move the `info!` inside the `move |new_value: String| { ... }` block so it only fires when `save_changes(new_value)` is actually called from `on_blur` or `on_keydown(Enter)`. Cosmetic but the noise actively obscures real save activity in logs (and confused the initial diagnosis of the GlobalSignal crash above).

The user-provided invite code therefore can't be used through this APK. content.subject: Verify member-info modal focus (was crash path)
content.description: Verified on Pixel 10 Pro XL. User opened the member-info modal; no SIGABRT, no "cannot access imported statics" panic. The `member_info_modal.rs:181` onmounted-focus call now routes through `crate::util::safe_spawn_local` and executes cleanly.

content.subject: Verify DM compose flow (was crash path)
content.description: Verified on Pixel 10 Pro XL. User opened DM thread (line 940 onmounted-focus path), composed and sent a message (line 524 compose flow), and opened the delete-confirm dialog (also line 940). No SIGABRT and no "cannot access imported statics" panic. All three `crate::util::safe_spawn_local` swaps in dm_thread_modal.rs execute cleanly.

content.subject: Verify nickname-edit blur (was crash path)
content.description: Verified that the spawn_local fix itself doesn't crash. The blur-on-Enter site at `nickname_field.rs:197` was never reached on device because a DIFFERENT pre-existing crash (GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed at dioxus-signals-0.7.9/src/global/mod.rs:100:46) fires earlier in the save chain. That crash is unrelated to spawn_local — filed separately. The spawn_local edit at line 197 is statically verified (cargo check clean on host + wasm32) and isolated to a code path that didn't execute because of the earlier panic.

content.subject: Wire Android clipboard via JNI (Copy buttons are no-ops)
content.description: Verified on Pixel 10 Pro XL after building + installing the patched APK: user confirmed "The Copy button works!" The JNI bridge in `ui/src/util.rs::android_copy_to_clipboard` (mirrors the `node_runtime::android_files_dir` pattern — pull JavaVM+Activity from ndk_context, attach thread, reflect Context.getSystemService("clipboard") → ClipData.newPlainText → setPrimaryClip) correctly writes the text into the system clipboard, where the user could paste it. Pre-fix behaviour was a no-op `let _ = text;` that silently swallowed every Copy.

content.subject: Fix GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname-save chain
content.description:
Pre-existing crash surfaced during Android verification on Pixel 10 Pro XL. Panic at `dioxus-signals-0.7.9/src/global/mod.rs:100:46` ("called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: AlreadyBorrowed(AlreadyBorrowedError)") on a nickname edit + Enter.

Sequence from logcat (`/tmp/claude/river-logcat.txt`, line 5569):
1. `Sending PutRequest for room MemberId(K53VLDBK)` (room_synchronizer.rs)
2. `Saving rooms to delegate storage` (chat_delegate.rs)
3. `Serialized request payload size: 131383 bytes`
4. Panic — `thread 'main' (4707) panicked at .../global/mod.rs:100:46`
5. SIGABRT

`nickname_field.rs::save_changes` already wraps its `ROOMS.with_mut` in `crate::util::defer`, so the immediate save delta is safe. The re-entrant borrow must be in the downstream chain triggered by `mark_needs_sync(owner_key)` — likely `save_rooms_to_delegate` reading a GlobalSignal while another mutation is still borrowed. Audit `save_rooms_to_delegate` and any use_effect / use_memo it triggers for unwrapped GlobalSignal reads (per AGENTS.md "Always use try_read()" rule).

Reproduction: edit a nickname in member-info modal, press Enter on Android (Pixel 10 Pro XL, current build). Unverified if web is affected.
content.activeForm: Pending: GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname save

content.subject: Move misleading "Saving nickname changes" log into closure body
content.description:
`nickname_field.rs:60` has `info!("Saving nickname changes");` inside the closure-creation block (around `let save_changes = { info!(...); ... move |new_value| { ... } }`), so it fires on every component re-render — i.e. every keystroke in the nickname input — not on actual saves. The 30+ log entries we saw in the verification logcat were all spurious re-renders, not actual save attempts.

Fix: move the `info!` inside the `move |new_value: String| { ... }` block so it only fires when `save_changes(new_value)` is actually called from `on_blur` or `on_keydown(Enter)`. Cosmetic but the noise actively obscures real save activity in logs (and confused the initial diagnosis of the GlobalSignal crash above).

content.subject: Verify rename + dark-mode on device
content.description: After the APK build completes: install on Pixel 10 Pro XL, force-stop + relaunch, check (a) the launcher icon label now says "River" not "RiverUi", and (b) toggling the system Dark theme (Settings → Display → Dark theme) swaps the app's colors automatically. If both work, commit and move on. If dark mode looks wrong on any screen, audit hard-coded `text-white` / `bg-red-500` etc. (the subagent flagged ~14 files).

toolUseResult.originalFile:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Apply River's Android overlay to the dx-generated module.
#
# dx (the Dioxus CLI) regenerates the Android module — manifest,
# MainActivity stub, etc. — every build. The Dioxus-managed way to add
# our own Kotlin code and tweak the manifest is to (a) keep the canonical
# files in `ui/android/`, and (b) re-apply them on top of the generated
# tree right before gradle assembles the APK. This script does (b).
#
# What it does (idempotent — safe to re-run on every build):
#   1. Copies every file under `ui/android/kotlin/` into the dx-generated
#      `src/main/kotlin/` directory, overwriting the stubs dx wrote there.
#   2. Patches `AndroidManifest.xml` to:
#      - Add `FOREGROUND_SERVICE` permission (INTERNET is already added
#        by dx).
#      - Add `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC` permission (required on
#        API 34+ for the `dataSync` foregroundServiceType; ignored on
#        older OS versions).
#      - Declare `<service android:name="dev.dioxus.main.RiverNodeService"
#        android:foregroundServiceType="dataSync" />` inside the
#        `<application>` element. `dataSync` is the closest stock
#        foreground-service type for a P2P node's background sync work
#        and is the only one compatible with the dx-generated
#        `compileSdk = 33`. If the project ever bumps compileSdk to 34+
#        we can switch to `specialUse` with a `freenet_p2p_node` subtype.
#
# The script writes only to `target/dx/`. It never touches `ui/android/`
# (the source-of-truth overlay) or anything outside the dx-generated
# Android module.

set -euo pipefail

# Where dx writes the Android module. Mirrors the path in
# `Makefile.toml`'s build-android task.
ANDROID_MODULE_DIR=${ANDROID_MODULE_DIR:-target/dx/river-ui/debug/android/app}
OVERLAY_DIR=${OVERLAY_DIR:-ui/android}

if [[ ! -d "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: dx-generated Android module not found at $ANDROID_MODULE_DIR" >&2
    echo "       Run 'cargo make build-android' once to generate it, then re-run this script." >&2
    exit 1
fi

if [[ ! -d "$OVERLAY_DIR" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: overlay source dir not found at $OVERLAY_DIR" >&2
    exit 1
fi

MANIFEST="$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml"
if [[ ! -f "$MANIFEST" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: AndroidManifest.xml not found at $MANIFEST" >&2
    exit 1
fi

echo "Applying River Android overlay…"
echo "  Overlay source:  $OVERLAY_DIR"
echo "  Module target:   $ANDROID_MODULE_DIR"

# 1. Copy overlay Kotlin / resources into the generated module.
#    `cp -R` preserves the directory layout (so dev/dioxus/main/*.kt
#    lands at src/main/kotlin/dev/dioxus/main/*.kt).
if [[ -d "$OVERLAY_DIR/kotlin" ]]; then
    cp -R "$OVERLAY_DIR/kotlin/." "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/kotlin/"
    echo "  ✓ Copied Kotlin overlay"
fi
if [[ -d "$OVERLAY_DIR/res" && -n "$(ls -A "$OVERLAY_DIR/res" 2>/dev/null)" ]]; then
    cp -R "$OVERLAY_DIR/res/." "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/res/"
    echo "  ✓ Copied res overlay"
fi

# 2. Patch the manifest. Each insertion is idempotent — we grep for
#    the entry first and only add if missing. This means re-running the
#    script after dx has regenerated a fresh manifest produces the same
#    result as running it the first time.
patch_manifest() {
    local pattern=$1
    local before=$2
    local insertion=$3

    if grep -q -F "$pattern" "$MANIFEST"; then
        return 0
    fi

    # Insert `$insertion` on the line BEFORE `$before`. macOS sed needs
    # the -i '' form; we use a portable Perl invocation instead so the
    # script runs the same on macOS and Linux CI.
    perl -i -pe "s|($before)|$insertion\n\$1|" "$MANIFEST"
}

# Add FOREGROUND_SERVICE + FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC permissions.
# We grep-test for each by full string so re-runs are no-ops.
patch_manifest \
    'android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE"' \
    '<application ' \
    '    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE" />'
patch_manifest \
    'android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC"' \
    '<application ' \
    '    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC" />'

# POST_NOTIFICATIONS is required on API 33+ for the foreground-service
# notification to be visible in the status bar. Without it the FGS still
# runs (Android allows the process to keep executing) but the user sees
# nothing — defeating the "ongoing presence" UX of the service.
# This is a runtime permission too: the user must grant it on first
# launch. The MainActivity overlay requests it via PermissionHelper.
patch_manifest \
    'android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS"' \
    '<application ' \
    '    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS" />'

# Declare the service inside <application>. Inserted on the line BEFORE
# `</application>` so the closing tag remains intact.
patch_manifest \
    '"dev.dioxus.main.RiverNodeService"' \
    '</application>' \
    '        <service android:name="dev.dioxus.main.RiverNodeService" android:exported="false" android:foregroundServiceType="dataSync" />'

echo "  ✓ Patched AndroidManifest.xml"
echo "Overlay applied successfully."

content.subject: Wire Android clipboard via JNI (Copy buttons are no-ops)
content.description: Verified on Pixel 10 Pro XL after building + installing the patched APK: user confirmed "The Copy button works!" The JNI bridge in `ui/src/util.rs::android_copy_to_clipboard` (mirrors the `node_runtime::android_files_dir` pattern — pull JavaVM+Activity from ndk_context, attach thread, reflect Context.getSystemService("clipboard") → ClipData.newPlainText → setPrimaryClip) correctly writes the text into the system clipboard, where the user could paste it. Pre-fix behaviour was a no-op `let _ = text;` that silently swallowed every Copy.

content.subject: Fix GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname-save chain
content.description:
Pre-existing crash surfaced during Android verification on Pixel 10 Pro XL. Panic at `dioxus-signals-0.7.9/src/global/mod.rs:100:46` ("called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: AlreadyBorrowed(AlreadyBorrowedError)") on a nickname edit + Enter.

Sequence from logcat (`/tmp/claude/river-logcat.txt`, line 5569):
1. `Sending PutRequest for room MemberId(K53VLDBK)` (room_synchronizer.rs)
2. `Saving rooms to delegate storage` (chat_delegate.rs)
3. `Serialized request payload size: 131383 bytes`
4. Panic — `thread 'main' (4707) panicked at .../global/mod.rs:100:46`
5. SIGABRT

`nickname_field.rs::save_changes` already wraps its `ROOMS.with_mut` in `crate::util::defer`, so the immediate save delta is safe. The re-entrant borrow must be in the downstream chain triggered by `mark_needs_sync(owner_key)` — likely `save_rooms_to_delegate` reading a GlobalSignal while another mutation is still borrowed. Audit `save_rooms_to_delegate` and any use_effect / use_memo it triggers for unwrapped GlobalSignal reads (per AGENTS.md "Always use try_read()" rule).

Reproduction: edit a nickname in member-info modal, press Enter on Android (Pixel 10 Pro XL, current build). Unverified if web is affected.
content.activeForm: Pending: GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname save

content.subject: Move misleading "Saving nickname changes" log into closure body
content.description:
`nickname_field.rs:60` has `info!("Saving nickname changes");` inside the closure-creation block (around `let save_changes = { info!(...); ... move |new_value| { ... } }`), so it fires on every component re-render — i.e. every keystroke in the nickname input — not on actual saves. The 30+ log entries we saw in the verification logcat were all spurious re-renders, not actual save attempts.

Fix: move the `info!` inside the `move |new_value: String| { ... }` block so it only fires when `save_changes(new_value)` is actually called from `on_blur` or `on_keydown(Enter)`. Cosmetic but the noise actively obscures real save activity in logs (and confused the initial diagnosis of the GlobalSignal crash above).

If both work, commit and move on. If dark mode looks wrong on any screen, audit hard-coded `text-white` / `bg-red-500` etc. (the subagent flagged ~14 files).

input.subject: Investigate: rooms multiply on every Android launch
input.description: User report (screenshot at /Users/sal/.claude/uploads/f1ed4c28-b6ce-4c57-a7e2-034b7f415590/b584170e-56716.png): "why do I keep getting more and more rooms when we launch even though I'm not adding any rooms?". Suggests duplicate room entries accumulating in the persisted delegate state across app restarts. Likely cause candidates: (1) example-data mode re-seeds rooms on every cold start without dedup, (2) legacy-delegate migration probe re-merges rooms each launch, (3) the room_list cache holds stale entries from previous sessions that never get pruned. Read the screenshot first; then audit cold-start hydration paths in `ui/src/components/app/chat_delegate.rs` (load + legacy migration), `ui/src/example_data.rs` (if it merges instead of replaces), and `ROOMS.with_mut` merge sites.

content.subject: Fix GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname-save chain
content.description:
Pre-existing crash surfaced during Android verification on Pixel 10 Pro XL. Panic at `dioxus-signals-0.7.9/src/global/mod.rs:100:46` ("called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: AlreadyBorrowed(AlreadyBorrowedError)") on a nickname edit + Enter.

Sequence from logcat (`/tmp/claude/river-logcat.txt`, line 5569):
1. `Sending PutRequest for room MemberId(K53VLDBK)` (room_synchronizer.rs)
2. `Saving rooms to delegate storage` (chat_delegate.rs)
3. `Serialized request payload size: 131383 bytes`
4. Panic — `thread 'main' (4707) panicked at .../global/mod.rs:100:46`
5. SIGABRT

`nickname_field.rs::save_changes` already wraps its `ROOMS.with_mut` in `crate::util::defer`, so the immediate save delta is safe. The re-entrant borrow must be in the downstream chain triggered by `mark_needs_sync(owner_key)` — likely `save_rooms_to_delegate` reading a GlobalSignal while another mutation is still borrowed. Audit `save_rooms_to_delegate` and any use_effect / use_memo it triggers for unwrapped GlobalSignal reads (per AGENTS.md "Always use try_read()" rule).

Reproduction: edit a nickname in member-info modal, press Enter on Android (Pixel 10 Pro XL, current build). Unverified if web is affected.

content.subject: Move misleading "Saving nickname changes" log into closure body
content.description:
`nickname_field.rs:60` has `info!("Saving nickname changes");` inside the closure-creation block (around `let save_changes = { info!(...); ... move |new_value| { ... } }`), so it fires on every component re-render — i.e. every keystroke in the nickname input — not on actual saves. The 30+ log entries we saw in the verification logcat were all spurious re-renders, not actual save attempts.

Fix: move the `info!` inside the `move |new_value: String| { ... }` block so it only fires when `save_changes(new_value)` is actually called from `on_blur` or `on_keydown(Enter)`. Cosmetic but the noise actively obscures real save activity in logs (and confused the initial diagnosis of the GlobalSignal crash above).

content.subject: Investigate: rooms multiply on every Android launch
content.description: User report (screenshot at /Users/sal/.claude/uploads/f1ed4c28-b6ce-4c57-a7e2-034b7f415590/b584170e-56716.png): "why do I keep getting more and more rooms when we launch even though I'm not adding any rooms?". Suggests duplicate room entries accumulating in the persisted delegate state across app restarts. Likely cause candidates: (1) example-data mode re-seeds rooms on every cold start without dedup, (2) legacy-delegate migration probe re-merges rooms each launch, (3) the room_list cache holds stale entries from previous sessions that never get pruned. Read the screenshot first; then audit cold-start hydration paths in `ui/src/components/app/chat_delegate.rs` (load + legacy migration), `ui/src/example_data.rs` (if it merges instead of replaces), and `ROOMS.with_mut` merge sites.

content.subject: Verify nickname-edit blur (was crash path)
content.description: Verified that the spawn_local fix itself doesn't crash. The blur-on-Enter site at `nickname_field.rs:197` was never reached on device because a DIFFERENT pre-existing crash (GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed at dioxus-signals-0.7.9/src/global/mod.rs:100:46) fires earlier in the save chain. That crash is unrelated to spawn_local — filed separately. The spawn_local edit at line 197 is statically verified (cargo check clean on host + wasm32) and isolated to a code path that didn't execute because of the earlier panic.

content.subject: Wire Android clipboard via JNI (Copy buttons are no-ops)
content.description: Verified on Pixel 10 Pro XL after building + installing the patched APK: user confirmed "The Copy button works!" The JNI bridge in `ui/src/util.rs::android_copy_to_clipboard` (mirrors the `node_runtime::android_files_dir` pattern — pull JavaVM+Activity from ndk_context, attach thread, reflect Context.getSystemService("clipboard") → ClipData.newPlainText → setPrimaryClip) correctly writes the text into the system clipboard, where the user could paste it. Pre-fix behaviour was a no-op `let _ = text;` that silently swallowed every Copy.

content.subject: Fix GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname-save chain
content.description:
Pre-existing crash surfaced during Android verification on Pixel 10 Pro XL. Panic at `dioxus-signals-0.7.9/src/global/mod.rs:100:46` ("called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: AlreadyBorrowed(AlreadyBorrowedError)") on a nickname edit + Enter.

Sequence from logcat (`/tmp/claude/river-logcat.txt`, line 5569):
1. `Sending PutRequest for room MemberId(K53VLDBK)` (room_synchronizer.rs)
2. `Saving rooms to delegate storage` (chat_delegate.rs)
3. `Serialized request payload size: 131383 bytes`
4. Panic — `thread 'main' (4707) panicked at .../global/mod.rs:100:46`
5. SIGABRT

`nickname_field.rs::save_changes` already wraps its `ROOMS.with_mut` in `crate::util::defer`, so the immediate save delta is safe. The re-entrant borrow must be in the downstream chain triggered by `mark_needs_sync(owner_key)` — likely `save_rooms_to_delegate` reading a GlobalSignal while another mutation is still borrowed. Audit `save_rooms_to_delegate` and any use_effect / use_memo it triggers for unwrapped GlobalSignal reads (per AGENTS.md "Always use try_read()" rule).

Reproduction: edit a nickname in member-info modal, press Enter on Android (Pixel 10 Pro XL, current build). Unverified if web is affected.
content.activeForm: Pending: GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname save

content.subject: Move misleading "Saving nickname changes" log into closure body
content.description:
`nickname_field.rs:60` has `info!("Saving nickname changes");` inside the closure-creation block (around `let save_changes = { info!(...); ... move |new_value| { ... } }`), so it fires on every component re-render — i.e. every keystroke in the nickname input — not on actual saves. The 30+ log entries we saw in the verification logcat were all spurious re-renders, not actual save attempts.

Fix: move the `info!` inside the `move |new_value: String| { ... }` block so it only fires when `save_changes(new_value)` is actually called from `on_blur` or `on_keydown(Enter)`. Cosmetic but the noise actively obscures real save activity in logs (and confused the initial diagnosis of the GlobalSignal crash above).

content.subject: Verify rename + dark-mode on device
content.description: After the APK build completes: install on Pixel 10 Pro XL, force-stop + relaunch, check (a) the launcher icon label now says "River" not "RiverUi", and (b) toggling the system Dark theme (Settings → Display → Dark theme) swaps the app's colors automatically. If both work, commit and move on. If dark mode looks wrong on any screen, audit hard-coded `text-white` / `bg-red-500` etc. (the subagent flagged ~14 files).

content.subject: Investigate: rooms multiply on every Android launch
content.description: User report (screenshot at /Users/sal/.claude/uploads/f1ed4c28-b6ce-4c57-a7e2-034b7f415590/b584170e-56716.png): "why do I keep getting more and more rooms when we launch even though I'm not adding any rooms?". Suggests duplicate room entries accumulating in the persisted delegate state across app restarts. Likely cause candidates: (1) example-data mode re-seeds rooms on every cold start without dedup, (2) legacy-delegate migration probe re-merges rooms each launch, (3) the room_list cache holds stale entries from previous sessions that never get pruned. Read the screenshot first; then audit cold-start hydration paths in `ui/src/components/app/chat_delegate.rs` (load + legacy migration), `ui/src/example_data.rs` (if it merges instead of replaces), and `ROOMS.with_mut` merge sites.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Apply River's Android overlay to the dx-generated module.
#
# dx (the Dioxus CLI) regenerates the Android module — manifest,
# MainActivity stub, etc. — every build. The Dioxus-managed way to add
# our own Kotlin code and tweak the manifest is to (a) keep the canonical
# files in `ui/android/`, and (b) re-apply them on top of the generated
# tree right before gradle assembles the APK. This script does (b).
#
# What it does (idempotent — safe to re-run on every build):
#   1. Copies every file under `ui/android/kotlin/` into the dx-generated
#      `src/main/kotlin/` directory, overwriting the stubs dx wrote there.
#   2. Patches `AndroidManifest.xml` to:
#      - Add `FOREGROUND_SERVICE` permission (INTERNET is already added
#        by dx).
#      - Add `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC` permission (required on
#        API 34+ for the `dataSync` foregroundServiceType; ignored on
#        older OS versions).
#      - Declare `<service android:name="dev.dioxus.main.RiverNodeService"
#        android:foregroundServiceType="dataSync" />` inside the
#        `<application>` element. `dataSync` is the closest stock
#        foreground-service type for a P2P node's background sync work
#        and is the only one compatible with the dx-generated
#        `compileSdk = 33`. If the project ever bumps compileSdk to 34+
#        we can switch to `specialUse` with a `freenet_p2p_node` subtype.
#
# The script writes only to `target/dx/`. It never touches `ui/android/`
# (the source-of-truth overlay) or anything outside the dx-generated
# Android module.

set -euo pipefail

# Where dx writes the Android module. Mirrors the path in
# `Makefile.toml`'s build-android task.
ANDROID_MODULE_DIR=${ANDROID_MODULE_DIR:-target/dx/river-ui/debug/android/app}
OVERLAY_DIR=${OVERLAY_DIR:-ui/android}

if [[ ! -d "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: dx-generated Android module not found at $ANDROID_MODULE_DIR" >&2
    echo "       Run 'cargo make build-android' once to generate it, then re-run this script." >&2
    exit 1
fi

if [[ ! -d "$OVERLAY_DIR" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: overlay source dir not found at $OVERLAY_DIR" >&2
    exit 1
fi

MANIFEST="$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml"
if [[ ! -f "$MANIFEST" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: AndroidManifest.xml not found at $MANIFEST" >&2
    exit 1
fi

echo "Applying River Android overlay…"
echo "  Overlay source:  $OVERLAY_DIR"
echo "  Module target:   $ANDROID_MODULE_DIR"

# 1. Copy overlay Kotlin / resources into the generated module.
#    `cp -R` preserves the directory layout (so dev/dioxus/main/*.kt
#    lands at src/main/kotlin/dev/dioxus/main/*.kt).
if [[ -d "$OVERLAY_DIR/kotlin" ]]; then
    cp -R "$OVERLAY_DIR/kotlin/." "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/kotlin/"
    echo "  ✓ Copied Kotlin overlay"
fi
if [[ -d "$OVERLAY_DIR/res" && -n "$(ls -A "$OVERLAY_DIR/res" 2>/dev/null)" ]]; then
    # The dx-generated module ships its default launcher as
    # `mipmap-*/ic_launcher.webp`. Our overlay ships `.png` at the same
    # basename — gradle treats `ic_launcher.webp` and `ic_launcher.png`
    # in the same density bucket as duplicate resources and fails the
    # build. Strip the .webp variants of any basename we're about to
    # overwrite, scoped to the overlay's res tree so we don't touch
    # unrelated dx resources.
    if find "$OVERLAY_DIR/res" -name "*.png" -print -quit | read -r; then
        for overlay_png in $(find "$OVERLAY_DIR/res" -name "*.png"); do
            rel_dir=$(dirname "${overlay_png#$OVERLAY_DIR/res/}")
            base=$(basename "$overlay_png" .png)
            dx_webp="$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/res/$rel_dir/$base.webp"
            if [[ -f "$dx_webp" ]]; then
                rm "$dx_webp"
            fi
        done
        echo "  ✓ Stripped dx .webp duplicates of overlay .png assets"
    fi
    cp -R "$OVERLAY_DIR/res/." "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/res/"
    echo "  ✓ Copied res overlay"
fi

# 2. Patch the manifest. Each insertion is idempotent — we grep for
#    the entry first and only add if missing. This means re-running the
#    script after dx has regenerated a fresh manifest produces the same
#    result as running it the first time.
patch_manifest() {
    local pattern=$1
    local before=$2
    local insertion=$3

    if grep -q -F "$pattern" "$MANIFEST"; then
        return 0
    fi

    # Insert `$insertion` on the line BEFORE `$before`. macOS sed needs
    # the -i '' form; we use a portable Perl invocation instead so the
    # script runs the same on macOS and Linux CI.
    perl -i -pe "s|($before)|$insertion\n\$1|" "$MANIFEST"
}

# Add FOREGROUND_SERVICE + FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC permissions.
# We grep-test for each by full string so re-runs are no-ops.
patch_manifest \
    'android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE"' \
    '<application ' \
    '    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE" />'
patch_manifest \
    'android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC"' \
    '<application ' \
    '    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC" />'

# POST_NOTIFICATIONS is required on API 33+ for the foreground-service
# notification to be visible in the status bar. Without it the FGS still
# runs (Android allows the process to keep executing) but the user sees
# nothing — defeating the "ongoing presence" UX of the service.
# This is a runtime permission too: the user must grant it on first
# launch. The MainActivity overlay requests it via PermissionHelper.
patch_manifest \
    'android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS"' \
    '<application ' \
    '    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS" />'

# Declare the service inside <application>. Inserted on the line BEFORE
# `</application>` so the closing tag remains intact.
patch_manifest \
    '"dev.dioxus.main.RiverNodeService"' \
    '</application>' \
    '        <service android:name="dev.dioxus.main.RiverNodeService" android:exported="false" android:foregroundServiceType="dataSync" />'

echo "  ✓ Patched AndroidManifest.xml"
echo "Overlay applied successfully."

Any specific advice about media queries, theme files, asset!() macro for stylesheets, or platform-specific styling for Android WebView?

content.content:
# Styling, Themes, and CSS in Dioxus 0.7

## CSS Variables for Theming

The documentation recommends using **CSS custom properties (variables)** for consistent theming. As stated: "This is generally preferred over using Rust variables since dynamic string formatting can be less efficient and harder to optimize."

The guide provides an example with root-level variables:

```css
:root {
    --color-primary: #3b82f6;
    --color-text: #1f2937;
    /* ... etc ... */
}
```

## Dark Mode & prefers-color-scheme

**The page does not address dark mode, `prefers-color-scheme`, or media queries specifically.** There is no guidance on responding to system theme preferences.

## CSS Imports & Stylesheets

Dioxus supports CSS importing through the `asset!()` macro. You can include stylesheets using `document::Stylesheet`:

```
static MAIN_CSS: Asset = asset!("/assets/main.css");
```

The documentation notes that using `document::Stylesheet` is preferred over regular `<link>` elements for server-side rendering optimization.

## SCSS & Tailwind Support

- **SCSS**: Supported directly via `asset!()` with `.scss` files
- **Tailwind**: Automatically detected and watched by DX; requires a `tailwind.css` file at the project root

## Platform-Specific Styling

**The page contains no information about Android WebView styling or platform-specific CSS approaches.**

content.subject: Fix GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname-save chain
content.description:
Pre-existing crash surfaced during Android verification on Pixel 10 Pro XL. Panic at `dioxus-signals-0.7.9/src/global/mod.rs:100:46` ("called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: AlreadyBorrowed(AlreadyBorrowedError)") on a nickname edit + Enter.

Sequence from logcat (`/tmp/claude/river-logcat.txt`, line 5569):
1. `Sending PutRequest for room MemberId(K53VLDBK)` (room_synchronizer.rs)
2. `Saving rooms to delegate storage` (chat_delegate.rs)
3. `Serialized request payload size: 131383 bytes`
4. Panic — `thread 'main' (4707) panicked at .../global/mod.rs:100:46`
5. SIGABRT

`nickname_field.rs::save_changes` already wraps its `ROOMS.with_mut` in `crate::util::defer`, so the immediate save delta is safe. The re-entrant borrow must be in the downstream chain triggered by `mark_needs_sync(owner_key)` — likely `save_rooms_to_delegate` reading a GlobalSignal while another mutation is still borrowed. Audit `save_rooms_to_delegate` and any use_effect / use_memo it triggers for unwrapped GlobalSignal reads (per AGENTS.md "Always use try_read()" rule).

Reproduction: edit a nickname in member-info modal, press Enter on Android (Pixel 10 Pro XL, current build). Unverified if web is affected.

content.subject: Move misleading "Saving nickname changes" log into closure body
content.description:
`nickname_field.rs:60` has `info!("Saving nickname changes");` inside the closure-creation block (around `let save_changes = { info!(...); ... move |new_value| { ... } }`), so it fires on every component re-render — i.e. every keystroke in the nickname input — not on actual saves. The 30+ log entries we saw in the verification logcat were all spurious re-renders, not actual save attempts.

Fix: move the `info!` inside the `move |new_value: String| { ... }` block so it only fires when `save_changes(new_value)` is actually called from `on_blur` or `on_keydown(Enter)`. Cosmetic but the noise actively obscures real save activity in logs (and confused the initial diagnosis of the GlobalSignal crash above).

content.subject: Verify rename + dark-mode on device
content.description: After the APK build completes: install on Pixel 10 Pro XL, force-stop + relaunch, check (a) the launcher icon label now says "River" not "RiverUi", and (b) toggling the system Dark theme (Settings → Display → Dark theme) swaps the app's colors automatically. If both work, commit and move on. If dark mode looks wrong on any screen, audit hard-coded `text-white` / `bg-red-500` etc. (the subagent flagged ~14 files).

content.subject: Investigate: rooms multiply on every Android launch
content.description: User report (screenshot at /Users/sal/.claude/uploads/f1ed4c28-b6ce-4c57-a7e2-034b7f415590/b584170e-56716.png): "why do I keep getting more and more rooms when we launch even though I'm not adding any rooms?". Suggests duplicate room entries accumulating in the persisted delegate state across app restarts. Likely cause candidates: (1) example-data mode re-seeds rooms on every cold start without dedup, (2) legacy-delegate migration probe re-merges rooms each launch, (3) the room_list cache holds stale entries from previous sessions that never get pruned. Read the screenshot first; then audit cold-start hydration paths in `ui/src/components/app/chat_delegate.rs` (load + legacy migration), `ui/src/example_data.rs` (if it merges instead of replaces), and `ROOMS.with_mut` merge sites.

About the Dioxus styling docs: the page covers the basics (CSS variables, `asset!` macro, `document::Stylesheet`, Tailwind/SCSS) but doesn't address dark mode, `prefers-color-scheme`, or Android WebView specifics. So our approach — Tailwind CSS variables + `<meta color-scheme>` + `WebSettingsCompat.setAlgorithmicDarkeningAllowed` on Android — isn't documented but is consistent with the underlying pattern they recommend. No tips we're missing from there.

if [[ -d "$OVERLAY_DIR/res" && -n "$(ls -A "$OVERLAY_DIR/res" 2>/dev/null)" ]]; then
    # For every file in our overlay tree, remove any same-basename file
    # in the target that has a DIFFERENT extension. Android's resource
    # merger treats `ic_launcher.png` and `ic_launcher.webp` in the same
    # density bucket as duplicates of the `ic_launcher` resource and
    # fails the build. The dx-generated tree ships defaults as .webp,
    # but a prior overlay run that placed .png files will leave them in
    # the target on subsequent builds (dx doesn't clean). This sweep
    # makes the overlay self-healing — pruning stale variants before
    # copying our canonical extension.
    while IFS= read -r -d '' overlay_file; do
        rel="${overlay_file#$OVERLAY_DIR/res/}"
        rel_dir=$(dirname "$rel")
        full_base=$(basename "$rel")
        base="${full_base%.*}"
        ext="${full_base##*.}"
        target_dir="$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/res/$rel_dir"
        if [[ -d "$target_dir" ]]; then
            for stale in "$target_dir/$base".*; do
                if [[ -f "$stale" && "${stale##*.}" != "$ext" ]]; then
                    rm "$stale"
                fi
            done
        fi
    done < <(find "$OVERLAY_DIR/res" -type f -print0)
    cp -R "$OVERLAY_DIR/res/." "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/res/"
    echo "  ✓ Copied res overlay (pruned stale duplicate-extension variants)"
fi

toolUseResult.originalFile:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Apply River's Android overlay to the dx-generated module.
#
# dx (the Dioxus CLI) regenerates the Android module — manifest,
# MainActivity stub, etc. — every build. The Dioxus-managed way to add
# our own Kotlin code and tweak the manifest is to (a) keep the canonical
# files in `ui/android/`, and (b) re-apply them on top of the generated
# tree right before gradle assembles the APK. This script does (b).
#
# What it does (idempotent — safe to re-run on every build):
#   1. Copies every file under `ui/android/kotlin/` into the dx-generated
#      `src/main/kotlin/` directory, overwriting the stubs dx wrote there.
#   2. Patches `AndroidManifest.xml` to:
#      - Add `FOREGROUND_SERVICE` permission (INTERNET is already added
#        by dx).
#      - Add `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC` permission (required on
#        API 34+ for the `dataSync` foregroundServiceType; ignored on
#        older OS versions).
#      - Declare `<service android:name="dev.dioxus.main.RiverNodeService"
#        android:foregroundServiceType="dataSync" />` inside the
#        `<application>` element. `dataSync` is the closest stock
#        foreground-service type for a P2P node's background sync work
#        and is the only one compatible with the dx-generated
#        `compileSdk = 33`. If the project ever bumps compileSdk to 34+
#        we can switch to `specialUse` with a `freenet_p2p_node` subtype.
#
# The script writes only to `target/dx/`. It never touches `ui/android/`
# (the source-of-truth overlay) or anything outside the dx-generated
# Android module.

set -euo pipefail

# Where dx writes the Android module. Mirrors the path in
# `Makefile.toml`'s build-android task.
ANDROID_MODULE_DIR=${ANDROID_MODULE_DIR:-target/dx/river-ui/debug/android/app}
OVERLAY_DIR=${OVERLAY_DIR:-ui/android}

if [[ ! -d "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: dx-generated Android module not found at $ANDROID_MODULE_DIR" >&2
    echo "       Run 'cargo make build-android' once to generate it, then re-run this script." >&2
    exit 1
fi

if [[ ! -d "$OVERLAY_DIR" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: overlay source dir not found at $OVERLAY_DIR" >&2
    exit 1
fi

MANIFEST="$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml"
if [[ ! -f "$MANIFEST" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: AndroidManifest.xml not found at $MANIFEST" >&2
    exit 1
fi

echo "Applying River Android overlay…"
echo "  Overlay source:  $OVERLAY_DIR"
echo "  Module target:   $ANDROID_MODULE_DIR"

# 1. Copy overlay Kotlin / resources into the generated module.
#    `cp -R` preserves the directory layout (so dev/dioxus/main/*.kt
#    lands at src/main/kotlin/dev/dioxus/main/*.kt).
if [[ -d "$OVERLAY_DIR/kotlin" ]]; then
    cp -R "$OVERLAY_DIR/kotlin/." "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/kotlin/"
    echo "  ✓ Copied Kotlin overlay"
fi
if [[ -d "$OVERLAY_DIR/res" && -n "$(ls -A "$OVERLAY_DIR/res" 2>/dev/null)" ]]; then
    cp -R "$OVERLAY_DIR/res/." "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/res/"
    echo "  ✓ Copied res overlay"
fi

# 2. Patch the manifest. Each insertion is idempotent — we grep for
#    the entry first and only add if missing. This means re-running the
#    script after dx has regenerated a fresh manifest produces the same
#    result as running it the first time.
patch_manifest() {
    local pattern=$1
    local before=$2
    local insertion=$3

    if grep -q -F "$pattern" "$MANIFEST"; then
        return 0
    fi

    # Insert `$insertion` on the line BEFORE `$before`. macOS sed needs
    # the -i '' form; we use a portable Perl invocation instead so the
    # script runs the same on macOS and Linux CI.
    perl -i -pe "s|($before)|$insertion\n\$1|" "$MANIFEST"
}

# Add FOREGROUND_SERVICE + FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC permissions.
# We grep-test for each by full string so re-runs are no-ops.
patch_manifest \
    'android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE"' \
    '<application ' \
    '    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE" />'
patch_manifest \
    'android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC"' \
    '<application ' \
    '    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC" />'

# POST_NOTIFICATIONS is required on API 33+ for the foreground-service
# notification to be visible in the status bar. Without it the FGS still
# runs (Android allows the process to keep executing) but the user sees
# nothing — defeating the "ongoing presence" UX of the service.
# This is a runtime permission too: the user must grant it on first
# launch. The MainActivity overlay requests it via PermissionHelper.
patch_manifest \
    'android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS"' \
    '<application ' \
    '    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS" />'

# Declare the service inside <application>. Inserted on the line BEFORE
# `</application>` so the closing tag remains intact.
patch_manifest \
    '"dev.dioxus.main.RiverNodeService"' \
    '</application>' \
    '        <service android:name="dev.dioxus.main.RiverNodeService" android:exported="false" android:foregroundServiceType="dataSync" />'

echo "  ✓ Patched AndroidManifest.xml"
echo "Overlay applied successfully."

content.subject: Verify nickname-edit blur (was crash path)
content.description: Verified that the spawn_local fix itself doesn't crash. The blur-on-Enter site at `nickname_field.rs:197` was never reached on device because a DIFFERENT pre-existing crash (GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed at dioxus-signals-0.7.9/src/global/mod.rs:100:46) fires earlier in the save chain. The spawn_local edit at line 197 is statically verified (cargo check clean on host + wasm32) and isolated to a code path that didn't execute because of the earlier panic.

content.subject: Wire Android clipboard via JNI (Copy buttons are no-ops)
content.description: Verified on Pixel 10 Pro XL after building + installing the patched APK: user confirmed "The Copy button works!" The JNI bridge in `ui/src/util.rs::android_copy_to_clipboard` (mirrors the `node_runtime::android_files_dir` pattern — pull JavaVM+Activity from ndk_context, attach thread, reflect Context.getSystemService("clipboard") → ClipData.newPlainText → setPrimaryClip) correctly writes the text into the system clipboard, where the user could paste it. Pre-fix behaviour was a no-op `let _ = text;` that silently swallowed every Copy.

content.subject: Fix GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname-save chain
content.description:
Pre-existing crash surfaced during Android verification on Pixel 10 Pro XL. Panic at `dioxus-signals-0.7.9/src/global/mod.rs:100:46` ("called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: AlreadyBorrowed(AlreadyBorrowedError)") on a nickname edit + Enter.

Sequence from logcat (`/tmp/claude/river-logcat.txt`, line 5569):
1. `Sending PutRequest for room MemberId(K53VLDBK)` (room_synchronizer.rs)
2. `Saving rooms to delegate storage` (chat_delegate.rs)
3. `Serialized request payload size: 131383 bytes`
4. Panic — `thread 'main' (4707) panicked at .../global/mod.rs:100:46`
5. SIGABRT

`nickname_field.rs::save_changes` already wraps its `ROOMS.with_mut` in `crate::util::defer`, so the immediate save delta is safe. The re-entrant borrow must be in the downstream chain triggered by `mark_needs_sync(owner_key)` — likely `save_rooms_to_delegate` reading a GlobalSignal while another mutation is still borrowed. Audit `save_rooms_to_delegate` and any use_effect / use_memo it triggers for unwrapped GlobalSignal reads (per AGENTS.md "Always use try_read()" rule).

Reproduction: edit a nickname in member-info modal, press Enter on Android (Pixel 10 Pro XL, current build). Unverified if web is affected.
content.activeForm: Pending: GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname save

content.subject: Move misleading "Saving nickname changes" log into closure body
content.description:
`nickname_field.rs:60` has `info!("Saving nickname changes");` inside the closure-creation block (around `let save_changes = { info!(...); ... move |new_value| { ... } }`), so it fires on every component re-render — i.e. every keystroke in the nickname input — not on actual saves. The 30+ log entries we saw in the verification logcat were all spurious re-renders, not actual save attempts.

Fix: move the `info!` inside the `move |new_value: String| { ... }` block so it only fires when `save_changes(new_value)` is actually called from `on_blur` or `on_keydown(Enter)`. Cosmetic but the noise actively obscures real save activity in logs (and confused the initial diagnosis of the GlobalSignal crash above).

content.subject: Verify rename + dark-mode on device
content.description: After the APK build completes: install on Pixel 10 Pro XL, force-stop + relaunch, check (a) the launcher icon label now says "River" not "RiverUi", and (b) toggling the system Dark theme (Settings → Display → Dark theme) swaps the app's colors automatically. If both work, commit and move on. If dark mode looks wrong on any screen, audit hard-coded `text-white` / `bg-red-500` etc. (the subagent flagged ~14 files).

content.subject: Investigate: rooms multiply on every Android launch
content.description: User report (screenshot at /Users/sal/.claude/uploads/f1ed4c28-b6ce-4c57-a7e2-034b7f415590/b584170e-56716.png): "why do I keep getting more and more rooms when we launch even though I'm not adding any rooms?". Suggests duplicate room entries accumulating in the persisted delegate state across app restarts. Likely cause candidates: (1) example-data mode re-seeds rooms on every cold start without dedup, (2) legacy-delegate migration probe re-merges rooms each launch, (3) the room_list cache holds stale entries from previous sessions that never get pruned. Read the screenshot first; then audit cold-start hydration paths in `ui/src/components/app/chat_delegate.rs` (load + legacy migration), `ui/src/example_data.rs` (if it merges instead of replaces), and `ROOMS.with_mut` merge sites.

content.description: Verified on Pixel 10 Pro XL. User opened the member-info modal; no SIGABRT, no "cannot access imported statics" panic. The `member_info_modal.rs:181` onmounted-focus call now routes through `crate::util::safe_spawn_local` and executes cleanly.

content.subject: Verify DM compose flow (was crash path)
content.description: Verified on Pixel 10 Pro XL. User opened DM thread (line 940 onmounted-focus path), composed and sent a message (line 524 compose flow), and opened the delete-confirm dialog (also line 940). content.subject: Verify nickname-edit blur (was crash path)
content.description: Verified that the spawn_local fix itself doesn't crash. The blur-on-Enter site at `nickname_field.rs:197` was never reached on device because a DIFFERENT pre-existing crash (GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed at dioxus-signals-0.7.9/src/global/mod.rs:100:46) fires earlier in the save chain. That crash is unrelated to spawn_local — filed separately. The spawn_local edit at line 197 is statically verified (cargo check clean on host + wasm32) and isolated to a code path that didn't execute because of the earlier panic.

content.subject: Wire Android clipboard via JNI (Copy buttons are no-ops)
content.description: Verified on Pixel 10 Pro XL after building + installing the patched APK: user confirmed "The Copy button works!" The JNI bridge in `ui/src/util.rs::android_copy_to_clipboard` (mirrors the `node_runtime::android_files_dir` pattern — pull JavaVM+Activity from ndk_context, attach thread, reflect Context.getSystemService("clipboard") → ClipData.newPlainText → setPrimaryClip) correctly writes the text into the system clipboard, where the user could paste it. Pre-fix behaviour was a no-op `let _ = text;` that silently swallowed every Copy.

content.subject: Fix GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname-save chain
content.description:
Pre-existing crash surfaced during Android verification on Pixel 10 Pro XL. Panic at `dioxus-signals-0.7.9/src/global/mod.rs:100:46` ("called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: AlreadyBorrowed(AlreadyBorrowedError)") on a nickname edit + Enter.

Sequence from logcat (`/tmp/claude/river-logcat.txt`, line 5569):
1. `Sending PutRequest for room MemberId(K53VLDBK)` (room_synchronizer.rs)
2. `Saving rooms to delegate storage` (chat_delegate.rs)
3. `Serialized request payload size: 131383 bytes`
4. Panic — `thread 'main' (4707) panicked at .../global/mod.rs:100:46`
5. SIGABRT

`nickname_field.rs::save_changes` already wraps its `ROOMS.with_mut` in `crate::util::defer`, so the immediate save delta is safe. The re-entrant borrow must be in the downstream chain triggered by `mark_needs_sync(owner_key)` — likely `save_rooms_to_delegate` reading a GlobalSignal while another mutation is still borrowed. Audit `save_rooms_to_delegate` and any use_effect / use_memo it triggers for unwrapped GlobalSignal reads (per AGENTS.md "Always use try_read()" rule).

Reproduction: edit a nickname in member-info modal, press Enter on Android (Pixel 10 Pro XL, current build). Unverified if web is affected.
content.activeForm: Pending: GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname save

content.subject: Move misleading "Saving nickname changes" log into closure body
content.description:
`nickname_field.rs:60` has `info!("Saving nickname changes");` inside the closure-creation block (around `let save_changes = { info!(...); ... move |new_value| { ... } }`), so it fires on every component re-render — i.e. every keystroke in the nickname input — not on actual saves. The 30+ log entries we saw in the verification logcat were all spurious re-renders, not actual save attempts.

Fix: move the `info!` inside the `move |new_value: String| { ... }` block so it only fires when `save_changes(new_value)` is actually called from `on_blur` or `on_keydown(Enter)`. Cosmetic but the noise actively obscures real save activity in logs (and confused the initial diagnosis of the GlobalSignal crash above).

content.subject: Verify rename + dark-mode on device
content.description: After the APK build completes: install on Pixel 10 Pro XL, force-stop + relaunch, check (a) the launcher icon label now says "River" not "RiverUi", and (b) toggling the system Dark theme (Settings → Display → Dark theme) swaps the app's colors automatically. If both work, commit and move on. If dark mode looks wrong on any screen, audit hard-coded `text-white` / `bg-red-500` etc. (the subagent flagged ~14 files).

content.subject: Investigate: rooms multiply on every Android launch
content.description: User report (screenshot at /Users/sal/.claude/uploads/f1ed4c28-b6ce-4c57-a7e2-034b7f415590/b584170e-56716.png): "why do I keep getting more and more rooms when we launch even though I'm not adding any rooms?". Suggests duplicate room entries accumulating in the persisted delegate state across app restarts. Likely cause candidates: (1) example-data mode re-seeds rooms on every cold start without dedup, (2) legacy-delegate migration probe re-merges rooms each launch, (3) the room_list cache holds stale entries from previous sessions that never get pruned. Read the screenshot first; then audit cold-start hydration paths in `ui/src/components/app/chat_delegate.rs` (load + legacy migration), `ui/src/example_data.rs` (if it merges instead of replaces), and `ROOMS.with_mut` merge sites.

content.text: **Found the real culprit!** The activity theme is hardcoded `Theme.AppCompat.Light.NoActionBar` — explicitly LIGHT. WebView's `prefers-color-scheme` follows the activity's theme, not the system's. Need to switch to `DayNight` which auto-follows the system.

input.content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
  Overlay for the activity theme so the WebView reports the system
  `prefers-color-scheme` correctly.

  dx generates `parent="@style/Theme.AppCompat.Light.NoActionBar"` —
  a hardcoded light theme. Even when the OS is in Dark mode, the
  activity stays light and the WebView reports
  `prefers-color-scheme: light` to the page (independent of
  `setAlgorithmicDarkeningAllowed` and any `<meta name="color-scheme">`
  on the page). Result: our tailwind.css's
  `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block never fired on Android.

  `DayNight.NoActionBar` is the AppCompat opt-in for system-driven
  light/dark, equivalent to `Theme.Material3.DayNight` for older
  AppCompat-based dx scaffolding. Required pair with the activity's
  `setAlgorithmicDarkeningAllowed(true)` call in MainActivity.kt.

  This file is rsync'd over the dx-generated module by
  `scripts/apply-android-overlay.sh`.
-->
<resources>
    <style name="AppTheme" parent="@style/Theme.AppCompat.DayNight.NoActionBar">
    </style>
</resources>

The blur-on-Enter site at `nickname_field.rs:197` was never reached on device because a DIFFERENT pre-existing crash (GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed at dioxus-signals-0.7.9/src/global/mod.rs:100:46) fires earlier in the save chain. That crash is unrelated to spawn_local — filed separately. The spawn_local edit at line 197 is statically verified (cargo check clean on host + wasm32) and isolated to a code path that didn't execute because of the earlier panic.

content.subject: Wire Android clipboard via JNI (Copy buttons are no-ops)
content.description: Verified on Pixel 10 Pro XL after building + installing the patched APK: user confirmed "The Copy button works!" The JNI bridge in `ui/src/util.rs::android_copy_to_clipboard` (mirrors the `node_runtime::android_files_dir` pattern — pull JavaVM+Activity from ndk_context, attach thread, reflect Context.getSystemService("clipboard") → ClipData.newPlainText → setPrimaryClip) correctly writes the text into the system clipboard, where the user could paste it. Pre-fix behaviour was a no-op `let _ = text;` that silently swallowed every Copy.

content.subject: Fix GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname-save chain
content.description:
Pre-existing crash surfaced during Android verification on Pixel 10 Pro XL. Panic at `dioxus-signals-0.7.9/src/global/mod.rs:100:46` ("called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: AlreadyBorrowed(AlreadyBorrowedError)") on a nickname edit + Enter.

Sequence from logcat (`/tmp/claude/river-logcat.txt`, line 5569):
1. `Sending PutRequest for room MemberId(K53VLDBK)` (room_synchronizer.rs)
2. `Saving rooms to delegate storage` (chat_delegate.rs)
3. `Serialized request payload size: 131383 bytes`
4. Panic — `thread 'main' (4707) panicked at .../global/mod.rs:100:46`
5. SIGABRT

`nickname_field.rs::save_changes` already wraps its `ROOMS.with_mut` in `crate::util::defer`, so the immediate save delta is safe. The re-entrant borrow must be in the downstream chain triggered by `mark_needs_sync(owner_key)` — likely `save_rooms_to_delegate` reading a GlobalSignal while another mutation is still borrowed. Audit `save_rooms_to_delegate` and any use_effect / use_memo it triggers for unwrapped GlobalSignal reads (per AGENTS.md "Always use try_read()" rule).

Reproduction: edit a nickname in member-info modal, press Enter on Android (Pixel 10 Pro XL, current build). Unverified if web is affected.

content.subject: Move misleading "Saving nickname changes" log into closure body
content.description:
`nickname_field.rs:60` has `info!("Saving nickname changes");` inside the closure-creation block (around `let save_changes = { info!(...); ... move |new_value| { ... } }`), so it fires on every component re-render — i.e. every keystroke in the nickname input — not on actual saves. The 30+ log entries we saw in the verification logcat were all spurious re-renders, not actual save attempts.

Fix: move the `info!` inside the `move |new_value: String| { ... }` block so it only fires when `save_changes(new_value)` is actually called from `on_blur` or `on_keydown(Enter)`. Cosmetic but the noise actively obscures real save activity in logs (and confused the initial diagnosis of the GlobalSignal crash above).

content.subject: Verify rename + dark-mode on device
content.description: After the APK build completes: install on Pixel 10 Pro XL, force-stop + relaunch, check (a) the launcher icon label now says "River" not "RiverUi", and (b) toggling the system Dark theme (Settings → Display → Dark theme) swaps the app's colors automatically. If both work, commit and move on. If dark mode looks wrong on any screen, audit hard-coded `text-white` / `bg-red-500` etc. (the subagent flagged ~14 files).

content.subject: Investigate: rooms multiply on every Android launch
content.description: User report (screenshot at /Users/sal/.claude/uploads/f1ed4c28-b6ce-4c57-a7e2-034b7f415590/b584170e-56716.png): "why do I keep getting more and more rooms when we launch even though I'm not adding any rooms?". Suggests duplicate room entries accumulating in the persisted delegate state across app restarts. Likely cause candidates: (1) example-data mode re-seeds rooms on every cold start without dedup, (2) legacy-delegate migration probe re-merges rooms each launch, (3) the room_list cache holds stale entries from previous sessions that never get pruned. Read the screenshot first; then audit cold-start hydration paths in `ui/src/components/app/chat_delegate.rs` (load + legacy migration), `ui/src/example_data.rs` (if it merges instead of replaces), and `ROOMS.with_mut` merge sites.

git add ui/src/components/app.rs \
        ui/android/kotlin/dev/dioxus/main/MainActivity.kt \
        ui/android/res/values/strings.xml \
        ui/android/res/values/styles.xml && \
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
feat(android): rename launcher to "River" and respect system dark theme

Three small Android-overlay additions that together fix three
user-visible defects on a freshly side-loaded build:

1. **Launcher / activity label** — dx auto-derived "RiverUi" from the
   `river-ui` crate name and wrote it into `strings.xml`. New
   overlay `ui/android/res/values/strings.xml` sets
   `<string name="app_name">River</string>`. Both `<application>`
   and `<activity>` in the dx manifest resolve `@string/app_name`,
   so one entry covers both surfaces. The notification dialog,
   recents card, and All Apps drawer entry all now read "River".

2. **System-driven dark mode** — required three pieces moving in
   lockstep, only the first of which was load-bearing:

   - `res/values/styles.xml` switches the activity's parent theme
     from `Theme.AppCompat.Light.NoActionBar` to
     `Theme.AppCompat.DayNight.NoActionBar`. THIS is what actually
     unblocked dark mode — WebView's `prefers-color-scheme` query
     follows the *activity's* UI mode, not the system's. With the
     activity locked light, the WebView reported `light` regardless
     of any other setting (verified by an in-WebView
     `matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches` probe
     that returned `false` until DayNight landed, then `true`).

   - `MainActivity.kt::onWebViewCreate` calls
     `WebSettingsCompat.setAlgorithmicDarkeningAllowed(webView.settings, true)`
     so the WebView doesn't algorithmically invert page colors and
     instead lets our CSS handle dark mode via the existing
     `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block in `tailwind.css`.

   - `app.rs` adds a `Meta { name: "color-scheme", content: "light dark" }`
     so the WebView treats the page as dark-aware (suppresses
     algorithmic inversion). The Dioxus `Meta` component injects via
     JS, which on a static page would be too late — but combined
     with `setAlgorithmicDarkeningAllowed(true)`, the WebView
     re-evaluates on meta-insertion.

   End-to-end verified on the Pixel 3a API 34 emulator in dark
   mode: probe returned `pcs:true, metas:1, bg:rgb(10,10,11)`
   (the `--color-bg: #0a0a0b` token from tailwind.css's dark block).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -5
